title: Taxi drivers rarely die of Alzheimer's — and what it tells us about cognitive reserve
description: Study suggests complex navigation and spatial orientation in professional taxi drivers builds strong cognitive reserve, protecting against Alzheimer's — relevant to behavioral economics and the value of cognitively demanding work in an AI-automated world.
notes: 274 points on HN. Key insight: cognitively demanding spatial navigation work may provide lifelong protective effects against neurodegenerative disease. Implications for AI displacement: jobs requiring complex real-world reasoning may offer irreplaceable human value.

title: How I use LLMs to learn complex topics
description: Popular HN post (607 points) on using LLMs as interactive tutors — Socratic dialogue, spaced repetition, concept mapping. Raises questions about learning methodology shifts and the future of education.
notes: 607 points — highest engagement today. Methods include iterative questioning, explaining concepts back, and generating practice problems. Could spark articles on AI-augmented learning methodologies.

title: Auto mode is now the default in Claude Code
description: Anthropic made autonomous agent mode the default for Claude Code. Signals the industry shift from human-assisted coding to AI-driven development workflows. Raises questions about quality, oversight, and developer skills.
notes: 173 points on HN. Major industry signal: AI coding agents going from opt-in to default. Implications for software engineering jobs, code quality, and the future of developer workflows.

title: Interaction Creates Dynamical AI Behavior Absent in Isolation
description: New physics paper shows AI agents in interaction adopt entirely new behavioral states not seen when running alone — like a boss AI driving a subordinate AI into an alien state. Simple kinetic theory model captures the effect.
notes: Published Aug 7, 2026. Counterintuitive finding: two AIs with same temperature parameter adopt a third behavioral state together. Bridges physics (kinetic theory) with AI agent interactions. Novel research direction.

title: Data Annotation as Measurement
description: Paper reframes data annotation as a measurement problem (not just agreement). Identifies 5 sources of annotation issues: error, ambiguity, impossibility, subjectivity, and annotator identity. Framework for improving data quality in AI training.
notes: AAAI/ACM AIES 2026. Grounded in measurement theory (N=132 lit review, N=10 interviews). Practical guidance for annotation teams. Could be relevant to topics around AI data quality, synthetic data, and training pipeline design.
